rows.question: Is 'volume' in dollars?
rows.answer: The candlestick docs define volume_fp as the number of contracts bought. The unit of the market-object volume_fp fields was not confirmed in the docs read, so they are shown as 'contracts (unit not confirmed)'. No dollar volume field was found.

rows.question: How are markets resolved as yes or no?
rows.answer: Each market's rules_primary text states the condition. Example: KXAAAGASD-26NOV19-3.7900 resolves Yes only if the AAA average is strictly greater than $3.79 on Nov 19, 2026. Result: no. Kalshi recorded expiration_value 3.7212, which matches AAA's Nov 19 average on the AAA page.

rows.question: What happens to a golf winner market if the golfer withdraws?
rows.answer: Per rules_secondary: tournament winner and end-of-round leader markets resolve to No; finishing position, make-the-cut, head-to-head and 3-ball markets resolve to Fair Market Value.

rows.question: How are BTC hourly markets settled?
rows.answer: The simple average of the sixty seconds of the CF Benchmarks Bitcoin Real-Time Index before 7 AM EST, taken at 7 AM EST on the stated date.

rows.question: What price-history granularity is available?
rows.answer: REST candlesticks offer 1-minute, 1-hour and 1-day periods, at most 5,000 periods per request.

rows.question: How many contracts are available at a given price?
rows.answer: The orderbook gives the resting quantity at each price level. Example, KXPGATOUR-THRC26-ZBAU (2026-11-20 capture): 60,548 contracts bid to buy YES at $0.001; 450 at $0.002. NO bids at $0.997 total 32,273.62 contracts, which equals 32,273.62 contracts available to buy YES at $0.003 (yes_ask_size on the market object).

suggestions.title: Suggestions for better decisions (for your choice; none implemented without approval)
suggestions.intro: Choose, per ID, one of: Approve, Defer, or Reject. Reply with the IDs and your choice. Until you decide, every suggestion stays 'Pending', and nothing here is applied to the site, data or trading.

rows.suggestion: Discover all open series in each topic automatically, instead of a fixed list, so culture and elections are fully covered.
rows.benefit: Fixes the culture gap (F-16) and widens elections coverage.
rows.information_needed: Full series list per category; paging cost.

rows.suggestion: Compute dollars traded per market from trade-level data (contracts times price), and rank by that.
rows.benefit: Answers the 'highest dollar amount' requirement directly (Q-01, F-13).

rows.suggestion: Add liquidity measures to the Liquidity page: spread (ask minus bid), depth within 1 and 5 cents of the best price, and the average price to buy N contracts from the book.
rows.benefit: Shows the cost to enter or exit a position, not only the quantity.

rows.suggestion: Add a WebSocket feed for second-level price charts.
rows.information_needed: Whether the public WebSocket needs authentication (UNVERIFIED).

rows.suggestion: Automatic settlement-source health check that flags any source whose name and URL do not match.
rows.benefit: Catches cases like F-02 to F-05 before a position depends on them.

rows.suggestion: Resolution tracker: store the last price before settlement and the yes or no outcome for every resolved market, and check how well prices predicted outcomes once enough markets have resolved.
rows.benefit: Tests whether market prices are well calibrated before any strategy is built on them.

rows.suggestion: Show the AAA national average and its daily change next to every gas strike.
rows.benefit: Gives the settlement reference beside each price.

rows.suggestion: Show the exchange status banner (exchange_active and trading_active) on every page.
rows.benefit: Avoids acting on prices while trading is paused.

rows.suggestion: Connect the demo account through a demo API key pair stored as a GitHub Actions secret, never in the repository, and build a portfolio snapshot job.
rows.benefit: Unblocks portfolio performance, trade analysis and strategy categories (T4).
rows.information_needed: A demo API key pair supplied by you through the secret store. This is a manual step on your side, and I cannot create it.

rows.suggestion: Record every trade with its definition fields (side, outcome side, price, contract count, fees, result, realized profit or loss) so that trades can be categorized later.
rows.benefit: Makes trade categories and strategy analysis reproducible.
rows.information_needed: Field definitions from the order and trade docs.

rows.suggestion: Pre-trade guardrails before any order: a maximum number of contracts per market, a maximum notional, a daily loss limit, and a kill switch.
rows.benefit: Limits losses from mistakes before any trading begins.
rows.information_needed: Your limit values (decision for you) and the order error codes.

rows.suggestion: Compare demo and production prices for the same tickers before any strategy is tested.
rows.benefit: Shows whether demo results carry over to production (Q-09).

rows.suggestion: Net each expected return of a trade against the official fee schedule before showing it.
rows.benefit: Stops gross edges from looking profitable when fees remove them (Q-10).
